key_insight: PrevizWhiz shows that low-fidelity 3D geometry plus 2D video references can effectively guide generative video models to produce usable previsualizations, removing the need for polished assets or deep 3D expertise. This hybrid input preserves spatial accuracy while keeping iteration fast and accessible.
problem_solved: Bridges the gap between imprecise hand-drawn storyboards and costly, expert-driven 3D previsualization by enabling rapid, spatially-aware video prototyping from rough 3D scenes and simple 2D footage.
method: Use rough 3D scenes as a spatial scaffold (simple geometry, camera paths, actor/bounding volumes) to encode scene layout and camera motion.
Condition a generative video model on the 3D scaffold plus 2D reference videos/frames to guide appearance, framing, and temporal coherence.
Provide an interactive loop for filmmakers to tweak 3D layout or reference clips and regenerate short previsualization sequences quickly.
impact: Enables faster creative iteration in film/animation pre-production and lowers technical barriers for filmmakers; for ML practitioners it highlights a practical conditioning strategy (spatial scaffold + 2D cues) for controllable generative video.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram: rough 3D scene + 2D reference → conditioning module → generated video frames.

paper_title: PrevizWhiz: Combining Rough 3D Scenes and 2D Video to Guide Generative Video Previsualization
paper_authors: Erzhen Hu, Frederik Brudy, David Ledo, George Fitzmaurice, Fraser Anderson
